note: Acceptance requirements; implementation and execution are separate. Offline/API evidence is never a browser E2E pass. Per-run reports record actual results.

scenarios.requirement: Neither required page exists: create exactly the two correctly typed pages with the exact paths and save their IDs.
Both pages already exist: reuse both IDs/permalinks, including valid non-helper pages with different titles; create zero checkout pages.
Only one required page exists: reuse it and create only the missing page.
Resume and start a second fresh run: checkout IDs, URLs and checkout-page count stay unchanged across all four configuration groups.
Draft/trash/wrong-content/path-collision/stale-registry cases: diagnose and recover an owned fixture or report the conflict; never silently use duplicate suffixes or the wrong checkout type.
Classic/Blocks switching: saved WooCommerce assignment, cart links, order-received and supported pay-for-order routes agree with the selected fixed checkout; reload and guest/customer journeys work.
Failure/interruption restoration returns original Woo page assignments and temporary edits, retains reusable checkout pages and allows another Prepare without duplication.
A subdirectory or new target resolves its own fixed pages and IDs without reusing another site's registry or losing the base path.
Fixed checkout discovery/create-missing-only, same IDs across runs, content/readiness validation, correct links and assignments, collision handling, restoration and target/base-path isolation.

Registry adoption/first setup, resume, next fresh run, one missing actor, collisions/role drift, cross-target and cross-run isolation. Assert stable IDs and counts, fresh access, restored actor baseline and no guest registration.
Sequential `Txc User N` labels on guest, registered and admin-created orders; sequence survives a new run and aborted submissions, and named order details survive later account-profile edits.

Admin creates one guest order (customer ID 0) and one order assigned to a reused customer in each matrix group. Enter billing/shipping details; add a product/variation and quantity; add supported shipping, fee or coupon; invoke actual supported TaxCloud/totals recalculation; compare visible/saved totals after reload. Complete via the configured trigger and verify remote ID, connection, customer, destinations, items and amounts.

Edit an uncaptured admin order's address/items/quantity and recalculate; apply/remove a saved exemption; save a draft without capture; cancel before capture; check post-capture edit restrictions and duplicate completion. Exercise the installed HPOS/legacy editor correctly; cover the other storage mode locally or on a suitable target and report its applicability.

In the dedicated QA runner's WordPress **Users → Profile** (`profile.php`), fill any required billing/purchaser details, actually submit a certificate, then View/Refresh/reload and verify the exact remote certificate/customer/state. This is WP own profile, distinct from frontend My Account. Do not submit under the human administrator's identity.

In **Users → Edit User** (`user-edit.php`) for a persistent QA customer, actually create the certificate; verify it attaches to the selected customer's ID rather than the acting admin. Reopen the customer's profile and frontend account to confirm authorized visibility and persistence.

As the reused customer, open **My Account → Exemption Certificates**, create and submit a certificate, view details, refresh, reload, and find the same ID in TaxCloud. Exercise empty/list/error states, cancel and double-submit protection; keep creation as a separate result from modal/validation checks.

Through classic checkout as registered customer and guest where offered, create an actual new exemption/single-purchase certificate, submit it, observe recalculated tax, place the order, and verify saved certificate ID, state/customer association and remote order exemption. Check guest certificate ownership and single-purchase reuse rules; do not expose one guest's certificate to another.

Repeat the actual creation/submission/application journey in Blocks checkout, including form validation, async loading, cancel/reselect, totals recalculation and order placement. Confirm it agrees with classic checkout; unavailable guest creation must be reported as an explicit applicability/feature gap.

Create through each supported management surface, then discover/apply the same saved certificate at eligible classic/Blocks checkout and admin order entry. Check its state restrictions, list refresh, expiry if supported, deletion/disabled behavior and no stale certificate after connection/API changes. Verify direct profile/account/order links cannot expose another customer's certificate.

Admin refunds storefront and admin-created orders, including guest and registered orders: full refund, two sequential partial item refunds, shipping-only, fee-only and mixed item/shipping/fee cases. Compare visible/saved/remote quantities, tax allocations, remaining refundable balance and status. Include a positive-tax case and rounding. Verify Woo refund ID, stable remote ID and no duplicate request/capture. Use manual/offline refund UI for the baseline.

Discover the actual customer refund/return/request UI supplied by this plugin/site. As the order's customer, initiate a full or partial refund/request, follow any required admin approval/rejection, and verify eventual Woo/TaxCloud state, customer-visible confirmation/history and request uniqueness. A request awaiting approval must not be called a completed refund or produce an early remote return. Include denied/duplicate requests and a guest journey only if the site provides authorized guest access.

A different customer, signed-out visitor or ineligible order status cannot request/execute an unauthorized refund; disabled/hidden controls and rejected server actions agree. Exercise any cancellation action separately from refund/return semantics. Check expired links/nonces locally or through supported normal UI recovery, without weakening auth.

My Account order list/detail, order received and authorized guest order links show correct named order, items/totals, payment/capture/refund state and addresses. Re-login/reload/back navigation preserves state. Pay-for-order or reorder flows are covered where offered; reorder creates a fresh named order/remote record and does not reuse the original capture/certificate improperly.

Double-click submission, form corrections, modal cancel/reopen, interrupted navigation and a rejected quote/capture/refund/certificate call recover without duplicate orders/certificates/returns. Inject deterministic failures locally; live failures retain their evidence and require outcome verification before any replay.

Reused actors across Realtime/Data Import and V1/V3 do not leak carts, API connection state, exemption selections or rate limits. Saved-address/profile changes produce fresh quotes and do not rewrite prior orders. Another run cannot operate on old records merely through a shared customer ID.

Customer/admin notices and supported order/refund/certificate notifications agree with the outcome and occur once. Use test mail capture/suppression to verify generated notifications without sending to real recipients; do not report mail delivery when only generation was observed. Validate notification links and guest/customer authorization where the test environment supports it.
